headline: Himachal: Russian paraglider gets stuck in high-tension electricity wires; rescued
content: Shimla, Nov 10 (PTI) A Russian paraglider in Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi, who got entangled in high-tension electricity wires over 100 metres above the ground, was rescued after a 3-hour-long operation on Tuesday, police said. The incident occurred today near Tandu, when Alexey (48) took off from Bir Billing and got stuck in the wires mid-flight. Following the incident, he immediately sent pictures of his location to the Bir Billing Paragliding Association to seek help. The association then alerted the district administration and dispatched rescue teams to the location. The rescue operation was jointly carried out by the teams of the National Highway Authority of India (NHAI), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Gawar Company. Considering the potential danger of falling, the teams also laid nets and mattresses on the road. Machinery, including a crane, was used to rescue the pilot. He was safely rescued following a three-hour-long rescue operation. He was taken to the Zonal hospital in Mandi, Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Chander Prakash said. PTI COR BPL APL

headline: Paraglider stranded on high-tension wires 150 metres above ground for 2.5 hours in Himachal Pradesh
content: SHIMLA: A paraglider was rescued after remaining suspended from high-tension power lines at a height of around 150 metres for nearly two-and-a-half hours in Himachal Pradesh's Mandi district on Tuesday.The administration used a 146-metre hydraulic crane to bring him to safety in a challenging rescue operation near Mehar village, around five kilometres from Mandi town.The pilot got entangled in the power lines along the Pathankot-Mandi highway in the afternoon. Other paragliders immediately alerted the administration, following which the power supply was switched off, an official said.Mandi SDM and police officials rushed to the spot, but rescuing the pilot from such a height posed a major challenge. The administration immediately arranged a 146-metre crane for the operation.An SDRF personnel used the crane's basket to reach the stranded paraglider and managed to bring him down safely.As a precautionary measure, people gathered at the spot spread a tarpaulin and mattresses on the ground beneath the stranded pilot in case he fell during the operation.The Pathankot-Mandi highway was closed to heavy vehicles while the crane was being assembled and the rescue operation was underway.Stay updated with the latest Shimla news. headline: Bunker Roy, founder of Barefoot College who empowered rural women, dies at 81
content: Sanjit Bunker Roy, the social activist who gave rural communities, particularly women, the skills and confidence to transform their villages without depending on formal education or conventional institutions, died on Tuesday at the age of 81.Roy, the founder of Barefoot College in Tilonia, Rajasthan, dedicated more than five decades to rural development and empowering marginalised communities. His funeral was held in Tilonia, where he had established the institution and made his home."Bunker Roy passed away peacefully at 6.15 am with Aruna Roy (wife) and others by his side. He went as he wanted to, in his own home in Tilonia, surrounded by some of the countless people who loved and cared for him deeply and passionately," the statement released by people close to him said.Like Mahatma Gandhi’s visit to Bihar in 1917 marked a foundational chapter in India’s freedom struggle, Roy’s life also changed after a visit to Palamu (now in Jharkhand) in 1965 famine acquainted him with poverty and hunger.Speaking at Ted Talks in 2011, Roy said, “The whole world was laid out for me. Everything was at my feet. Then I thought out of curiosity to see what a village looks like. In 1965 I went to what is called the worst Bihar famine and I saw starvation, death and hunger for the first time.”Author Amitav Ghosh recalled that Roy was a champion squash player and could have been a top diplomat, bureaucrat or corporate honcho but instead he chose to dedicate his life to alleviating poverty in rural India. “He was a true hero,” he said.Barefoot College trains marginalised illiterate and semi-literate women from the Global South to become Solar Engineers. They learn how to design, make, install and repair solar lanterns and home-lighting systems and have become affectionately known as “Solar Mamas”. The organisation follows a Gandhian philosophy that believes technology should be demystified and there is a difference between literacy and education.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said, “By founding the Barefoot College in Tilonia, Rajasthan, he transcended conventional notions of formal education, proving that illiterate and semi-literate villagers, especially women, possessed the wisdom, skill and capability to build, innovate and lead. His extraordinary vision of training rural grandmothers into "Barefoot Solar Engineers" illuminated thousands of off-grid homes across India and the developing world, leaving behind an indelible legacy of dignity, community empowerment, and environmental stewardship,” he said.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh recalled Roy playing a key role in creating vast new opportunities for what were then called 'voluntary agencies' in development schemes and programmes.“This was at the personal initiative of former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi. Bunker Roy became a close associate of Sam Pitroda also in the implementation of the various Technology Missions especially in drinking water, immunisation and adult literacy. In later years, he would smilingly say that he was recognised as being the husband of the legendary Aruna Roy, who had resigned from the IAS in the mid-1970s to join him in Tilonia. Her 2024 memoir, The Personal is Political, is a wonderful account of their journey together,” Ramesh said.

headline: SC orders SIT probe into illegal gravel mining in Rajasthan’s Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers
content: The Supreme Court has ordered a probe by a Special Investigation Team (SIT) into illegal bajri (gravel) mining in Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers and their tributaries in Rajasthan.While directing the Rajasthan Government to set up an SIT to investigate illegal mining, a Bench led by Justice Vikram Nath also ordered a probe into the alleged involvement of public officials in facilitating such illegal activities.The SIT will examine if public officials facilitated or enabled illegal mining, including instances of collusion, dereliction of duty or failure to act despite knowledge of violations. Appropriate action has to be initiated against those found responsible.The Bench — which also included Justice Sandeep Mehta — directed the SIT to file a status report before it on or before the next date of hearing on November 27.It restrained the state government from granting permissions for the establishment of new industrial units along or in the vicinity of the riverine ecosystem until the High Flood Line and buffer zones are scientifically determined.It said the SIT shall be headed by an officer not below the rank of Inspector General of Police and will include the Superintendents of Police of Jodhpur, Balotra and Pali.“The SIT shall undertake a comprehensive investigation into organised illegal bajri mining activities affecting the Luni, Jojari and Bandi rivers and their tributaries. The investigation shall extend to identifying the persons and entities involved in such activities, the networks through which the illegal extraction, transportation and sale of bajri are organised, and the beneficiaries of such operations,” it said in its October 26 order.The order came during the hearing of a suo motu case on pollution in the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system, affecting the environment and the lives of approximately 20 lakh people.Earlier, the Bench had warned Rajasthan authorities of a CBI probe into alleged illegal mining and the regularisation of mining areas along the Jojari-Luni-Bandi river system. It had sought to know why the state authorities granted mining leases in areas where illegal mining had been detected, and regularising illegal leases.It ordered that an additional protective zone of 100 metres be maintained on either side of the respective recorded outer boundaries of the rivers. The Court held that No Red Category industry shall be permitted to be established within a distance of 500 metres from the said recorded outer boundaries.The Bench expressed serious concern over the Rajasthan Mining Department's explanation that mining leases had been subsequently granted according to prescribed procedures in several areas where illegal gravel mining had previously been detected.“The fact that mining leases may have subsequently been granted in accordance with the prescribed procedure does not, by itself, answer the question whether the grant of such leases is environmentally sustainable or consistent with the need to preserve and restore the natural course, riverbed and ecological integrity of the river systems,” it said, adding the authorities attempted to legitimise illegal mining activities through subsequent lease grants instead of taking appropriate action against those responsible.The Bench said it would consider directing appropriate action against officers found responsible for permitting or facilitating such activities.“We deprecate the apparent attempt on the part of the Mining Department of the State of Rajasthan to legitimise illegal mining activities being carried out in the riverbeds by subsequently granting mining leases, rather than taking appropriate action against those responsible. We shall consider directing appropriate action against the officers found responsible for permitting or facilitating such activities,” it said.

headline: NIT Raipur Lays Foundation Stone for ₹88.76-Crore Centre of Excellence to Boost Innovation and Entrepreneurship
content: National Institute of Technology Raipur on Tuesday laid the foundation stone for the ₹88.76-crore Smt. Mithilesh Agrawal Centre of Excellence for Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Engineering and Technology (MACIEET), marking a significant step towards strengthening Chhattisgarh's innovation, research and startup ecosystem. The centre is being established through a joint initiative of the Motilal Oswal Foundation, the Government of Chhattisgarh and NIT Raipur, with funding shared in the ratio of 80:10:10. The Motilal Oswal Foundation will contribute ₹71.008 crore, while the State Government and NIT Raipur will contribute ₹8.876 crore each. The project will be implemented through the NIT Raipur Foundation for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (NITRRFIE), a Section 8 company of the institute. Named after Smt. Mithilesh Agrawal, mother of Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited Chairman and Co-founder Shri Raamdeo Agrawal, the centre is envisioned as a comprehensive hub for advanced technology, skill development, research, incubation and entrepreneurship. Shri Raamdeo Agrawal hails from Nagpura village near Raipur. The foundation stone ceremony was attended by Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai, Shri Raamdeo Agrawal, Chairman and Co-founder of Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited, Dr. Suresh Haware, Chairman of the Board of Governors of NIT Raipur, and Dr. N. V. Ramana Rao, Director of NIT Raipur. Registrar Ashok K. Gupta, Dr. Sameer Bajpai, Head of the Career Development Centre, Dr. Anuj K. Shukla, Faculty-in-Charge of NITRRFIE, Dhamtari District Magistrate Shri Avinash Mishra, and other faculty members, officials, alumni, students and distinguished guests were also present. Designed by INI Design Studio around the concept of a 'Learning Street', the centre will be a ground-plus-six-storey building spread across a built-up area of approximately 12,307 square metres. The L-shaped structure will feature a landscaped courtyard, an open-air amphitheatre, a double-skin façade for climate control and rooftop solar panels. The design also incorporates existing trees on the site, with a focus on sustainability and an environment-friendly campus. Addressing the gathering, Chief Minister Shri Vishnu Deo Sai said MACIEET would provide the youth of Chhattisgarh with access to world-class laboratories, mentoring and incubation facilities within the State. He said the State Government was proud to be associated with the initiative, which would help transform young people's ideas into enterprises and employment opportunities, while advancing the vision of Viksit Chhattisgarh and Viksit Bharat.

headline: Himachal: Baddi Police form special teams to nab accused in Nalagarh firing incident; one injured
content: Nalagarh (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 10 (ANI): The Baddi Police have constituted special teams to arrest a man accused of opening fire on another person near the Lakad Depot on Ramshahar Road in Nalagarh on Tuesday.The victim, identified as Mohammad Aslam alias Ballu, sustained gunshot injuries in the incident.According to the police, the incident took place within the jurisdiction of Nalagarh Police Station. Aslam, son of Ghulam Rasool and a resident of Ward No. 7, Nalagarh, was rushed to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Nalagarh, for medical treatment.On the basis of a complaint lodged by Joginder Singh, son of Santokh Singh, a resident of village Pannar in Nalagarh tehsil, police registered a case under Sections 109 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 25, 54 and 59 of the Arms Act.As per the complaint, the accused, identified as Sahil, son of Rajender Singh and a resident of Nalagarh, allegedly fired multiple shots at Aslam before fleeing the spot on a motorcycle.Taking serious note of the incident, Baddi Superintendent of Police Vinod Kumar (Vinod Dhiman, as mentioned in the press release) visited the crime scene and reviewed the situation. He also directed police officials to take immediate steps to apprehend the accused.Superintendent of Police Baddi Vinod Kumar said that "We have constituted multiple special police teams to ensure the early arrest of the accused. The teams are investigating all aspects of the incident and conducting searches at possible hideouts. Efforts are underway to apprehend the accused at the earliest."Police said that the investigation into the case was in progress and teams were pursuing various leads to trace and arrest the accused. (ANI)

headline: Sukhu Launches 26 Projects Worth Rs. 1.75 bn in Chamba
content: Sukhu formed a committee to discuss with the Centre the demand for Scheduled Tribe status for 27 gram panchayats in the constituency. He announced that the state government would soon introduce the Mukhya Mantri Ka Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar Yojana, which will cover more than 300,000 families with annual incomes below Rs. 75,000. Under the proposed scheme, eligible women aged 21 to 59 will receive monthly assistance of Rs. 1,500. The package will also provide 300 units of free electricity and health insurance coverage of Rs. 1 mn, according to officials. The chief minister announced Rs. 180 mn for construction of the Holi-Utrala road and said CBSE-affiliated schools would open at Lylh, Mehla, Bharmour, Sunara and Holi from the next academic session. The government will also examine proposals to upgrade schools at Churi, Chadi, Ananaihar, Grundhi and Kunaid, and assess a suitable location for a helipad. Among the completed works was a Model Degree College at Lylh Kothi, built at a cost of Rs. 144.6 mn. Officials said the upgraded Bharmour-Badgram via Gaagal to Luni road and the Sirdi-Supa road cost Rs. 106.4 mn and Rs. 96.5 mn, respectively. New road projects include Nayagram-Bajol at Rs. 112.6 mn, Lamu-Quarsi at Rs. 169.8 mn and Kandi-Kuther at Rs. 119.8 mn, while a 30-bed hospital building at Choori Community Health Centre will cost Rs. 56.4 mn. Sukhu criticised the previous BJP government for inadequate attention to health, education and road connectivity in the constituency. headline: Burning Fields, Choking Cities: North India’s Air Pollution Crisis Crosses Borders
content: New Delhi/Shimla: The arrival of November has once again brought a familiar but alarming environmental crisis to northern India. Thick layers of smog have enveloped Delhi and several cities in Punjab and Haryana, while Lahore and other parts of Pakistan’s Punjab province are also struggling with deteriorating air quality. Adding to the regional concern, industrial towns in Himachal Pradesh, particularly Baddi, are witnessing a worrying rise in pollution levels, challenging the perception that the hill state is relatively insulated from the air-quality crisis affecting the northern plains. The crisis is being driven by multiple factors, including agricultural residue burning, Diwali firecracker emissions, vehicular exhaust, industrial pollution, construction dust and unfavourable meteorological conditions. The combined effect has pushed several urban and industrial centres into unhealthy air-quality categories. What makes the situation particularly concerning is that pollution is no longer an isolated problem affecting Delhi or a few industrial cities. It has become a regional environmental challenge involving the entire northwestern plains and neighbouring areas across the international border. For millions of residents, the consequences are increasingly visible in everyday life: hazy skies, reduced visibility, irritation in the eyes and throat, breathing difficulties and growing concerns over long-term health consequences. The national capital has once again emerged as the centre of the regional air pollution crisis. Following Diwali celebrations, Delhi witnessed a sharp deterioration in air quality, with the CPCB recording an average Air Quality Index (AQI) of 376 on November 9, placing it in the ‘very poor’ category. Several areas experienced even worse conditions, with independent monitoring platforms reporting exceptionally high readings. The combination of firecracker emissions, agricultural smoke, vehicular pollution and industrial activities contributed to the deterioration.
